w:r.w:t: TEACHER’S VERSION — answers, model answers and teaching notes are printed in red.
Proofread the following sentences. Each sentence contains TWO errors.
In recent years, food delivery apps has became an indispensable part of daily life for busy office workers.
It is undeniable that early childhood education play a pivotal role in shape children’s characters.
To begin with, cultural exchange programme offer students golden opportunity to broaden their horizon.
From the perspective of parents, school counselling services allow it to understand their children better, which in turn strengthen family relationships.
School libraries serve as a powerful mean of encourage students to read, which enables them to become lifelong learners.
Admittedly, e-books are more convenience; nevertheless, printed books remain irreplaceable, as reading on paper help readers to concentrate better.
THE BASIC SENTENCES STUDENTS USUALLY WRITE
The government can build more sports facilities.
Schools can organise more sports activities and sports days.
Parents can exercise with their children at weekends.
There is an urgent need for [doer] to [base verb phrase].
The government can build more sports facilities.
There is an urgent need for
in free, accessible sports facilities in every district.

“There is an urgent need for” is followed by [doer] + TO + base verb — never the base verb on its own (“for the government invest”) or a gerund (“for the government investing”). Use it when the problem cannot wait; “pressing” and “growing” can replace “urgent”.
To [goal], [doer] should make it a priority to [base verb phrase].
Schools can organise more sports activities and sports days.
add a daily exercise break to the timetable.
“make it a priority to” takes the BASE verb (“to add”, never “to adding”). Opening with “To + goal” replaces the vague “so that” and shows the marker your purpose in the first three words.
[Doer], in collaboration with [second party], should [verb phrase].
Parents can exercise with their children at weekends.
should encourage their children to adopt a more active lifestyle.

“in collaboration with” = working together with. It is far stronger than “and” or “also” and shows the marker that you understand shared responsibility. The doer is swappable: “The government, in collaboration with district councils, should …”.

the three patterns are deliberately kept to ONE clause. Endings of the “, so as to …” / “, thereby + –ing” type were left out this time — level 3 students lose control of the main clause as soon as they open a second one. Add the endings back only when the class can hold the short form.

Upgrade each simple sentence with the pattern shown, and keep the pattern to ONE clause, as taught in Part C. The topics are different from the fitness topic in Part C. Sets 4–6 are more challenging: you must join the TWO simple sentences into ONE upgraded sentence.
The government can tell teenagers about the importance of sleep.
There is an urgent need for the government to raise teenagers’ awareness of the importance of sleep.
Accept any sensible base verb phrase: “launch a campaign on healthy sleeping habits”, “make sleep education part of the junior curriculum”.
Set 2. Topic: Food Waste on Campus
Schools can ask students not to waste food in the canteen.
To cut food waste on campus, schools should make it a priority to offer smaller portions and free second helpings.
Accept “To reduce food waste …” and any sensible verb phrase after “make it a priority to”.
Parents can talk to their children about cyberbullying.
Parents, in collaboration with schools, should discuss online safety openly with their children.
Accept any sensible second party (the school, social workers) and any formal verb phrase (“set clear rules about online behaviour at home”).
Set 4. Topic: Youth Mental Health (more challenging)
The government can spend more money on mental health services.
Young people need these services at school.
There is an urgent need for the government to invest more in school-based mental health services for young people.
Idea 2 is folded into the modifier “school-based”, so the pattern stays one clean clause. Also accept “… invested more in mental health services in schools.”
Set 5. Topic: Declining Reading Habits (more challenging)
Schools can keep the library open after school.
Students need a quiet place to read.
To give students a quiet place to read, schools should make it a priority to keep the library open after school.
Idea 2 becomes the fronted goal; the second plain sentence must disappear into the pattern.
Set 6. Topic: Care for the Elderly (more challenging)
Teenagers can visit elderly neighbours who live alone.
Community centres can arrange these visits.
Teenagers, in collaboration with community centres, should organise regular visits to elderly neighbours who live alone.
Idea 2 becomes the second party after “in collaboration with”. Watch the plural: “the elderly” is already plural — never “the elderlies”.

A recent survey has found that young people in Hong Kong take far less exercise than they should, and the government is now inviting ideas on how to improve their physical well-being. Write a letter to the editor of the Hong Kong Young Post, suggesting ONE way in which our city can improve the physical well-being of its young people.
Make ONE suggestion (100 words) about improving physical
open your paragraph with ONE of today’s three patterns as the topic sentence.
Follow the chain: [Topic sentence] → [Explain] → [Example / evidence] → [Round off].
Teacher’s three suggested paragraphs — any ONE of them answers the task
Suggested paragraph 1 — the government (topic sentence uses Pattern 1)
There is an urgent need for the government to invest in free, accessible sports facilities in every district.
Young people are not lazy; the problem is that the nearest pitch is often booked out months in advance, and a private gym costs more than most families can spare.

Take a Form 5 student in Kwun Tong: with a floodlit running track and a basketball court five minutes from home, an hour of exercise becomes the easiest part of her evening instead of a two-bus journey.
Facilities within walking distance turn good intentions into daily habits, and that is the cheapest health policy a city can buy.
Suggested paragraph 2 — schools (topic sentence uses Pattern 2)
To boost students’ physical fitness, schools should make it a priority to add a daily exercise break to the timetable.
Two PE lessons a week cannot undo six hours of sitting still, and students who never move at school rarely choose to move afterwards, however warmly their teachers praise a healthy lifestyle.
Fifteen minutes of skipping, badminton or jogging before the first lesson would give every student — not only the team players — a daily dose of activity.
Such a break costs the timetable fifteen minutes and buys students a lifetime of healthier habits.
Suggested paragraph 3 — parents (topic sentence uses Pattern 3)
Parents, in collaboration with schools, should encourage their children to take up a sport and stick with it.
Children copy what they see at home, and enthusiasm for a new sport fades quickly when nobody joins in, drives them to practice or turns up to watch.
A weekend hike, a family badminton session in the park, or simply a parent cheering from the sidelines turns a hobby into a habit that no textbook can teach.
Active families raise active young people, and that habit outlasts any school programme or government campaign.
each paragraph makes ONE suggestion; the topic sentence is the only place where a pattern is required. Check the chain [Topic sentence] → [Explain] → [Example / evidence] → [Round off].
